subject: AuroraForge private cluster — sudden throughput regression and 500s (needs runbook + exec sync)
messages:
From: Sara Patel <sara.patel@auroraforge.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: Amit Rao <amit.rao@auroraforge.com>
Date: 2028-03-02T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick — production errors on our private cluster

Naomi,

We're seeing a sharp regression across our private VPC deployment that started ~08:40 PT this morning. Key symptoms: overall throughput down ~40% for normal traffic, p95 latency jumped from ~320ms to ~1.6s, and we're getting intermittent 500/502 model-decode errors for streaming endpoints. The errors are concentrated on 3 out of 12 hosts in our pool.

We've attached a Grafana snapshot and the error tail (short) — logging shows repeated "kv-cache-miss -> fallthrough decode" flows and large GC-like stalls on the same hosts. We rolled a small quantization patch last week (recommended by your onboarding notes) but this seemed stable until today.

Customer impact: several paying customers are reporting timeouts; one key integration timed out during a demo. We need an ops runbook and an ETA for mitigation. This is now flagged for our execs; they want a remediation plan and whether we should consider failover to Hosted fallback while you investigate.

Can you escalate and confirm next steps?

Thanks,
Sara
Sara Patel
Director, Platform Engineering
AuroraForge

Attachments: auroraforge_grafana_snapshot.png (png, 168kb); error_tail_03-02.txt (text, 24kb)

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Sara Patel <sara.patel@auroraforge.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-02T09:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick — production errors on our private cluster

Sara — thanks for the heads up and the attachments. We're treating this as high priority. Initial read: the symptoms (host-localized 500s + kv-cache misses + a recent quantization change) point to either a kernel/runtime scheduling regression on those hosts or a KV cache eviction/compaction policy that's interacting poorly with longer context traces.

Immediate actions (my side):
- Opening an incident bridge (link to be shared) and pulling on-call runtime and infra.
- Asking infra to cordon the three bad hosts from new traffic and trigger a graceful restart so they drop any poisoned caches.
- Engineering (Vivek) — can you confirm whether the quantization patch included any kernel-level op changes that could affect memory compaction? If yes, we may want to roll that patch back on the affected pool while we debug.
- Marissa, can you prepare a short canary/fallback plan (enable Hosted fallback + fail traffic for 15 min) and an ask for commercial (credits/exec message) if customers need immediate remediation?

Sara — we'll keep this tight. Would you be available for a 30-min sync at 10:00 PT to brief your execs and coordinate a failover if needed?

Naomi Feldman
Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Sara Patel <sara.patel@auroraforge.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-02T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick — production errors on our private cluster

Naomi / Sara — I joined the bridge and pulled the runtime logs from the affected hosts. Quick notes:
- The quantization patch (applied 2028-02-24) added an optional fused-kernel path for rotary-attention. The path is gated by a flag; the flag should not be enabled by default.
- On the three hosts we see the fused path active and a steady climb in per-request CPU microstalls when sequence length > 1024. That correlates with the p95 spike.
- There's also a KV cache compaction job that runs every 30m; these hosts show compaction finishing at ~08:42 which correlates exactly with the first spike in errors. Hypothesis: compaction is corrupting/invalidating some cache entries under the fused path, causing retry/decode fallthroughs and occasional 500s.

Immediate remediation plan (proposed):
1) Disable fused-kernel flag across the pool (target: 08:50 PT) — quick config flip and rolling restart of workers on the three hosts.
2) Temporarily pause KV compaction on the pool and re-run compaction offline to validate integrity.
3) If step 1/2 reduces errors, schedule a targeted kernel rollback for the patched build and open a postmortem.
4) Short-term: enable Hosted fallback for the affected customer traffic for up to 1 hour during the fix window.

I can start step 1 immediately once Naomi signs off. Marissa — can you confirm the fallback enable path and any billing/credit impacts? Also adding a small runbook doc (attached) with the exact commands — please follow those steps; they are destructive to live cache.

Vivek
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Attachments: runbook_auroraforge_v1.2.pdf (pdf, 48kb)

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Sara Patel <sara.patel@auroraforge.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-03T14:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick — production errors on our private cluster

Sara — quick post-mortem / status update after today's remediation window: we executed Vivek's plan. Summary:
- 10:05 PT: disabled fused-kernel flag and rolled the three hosts. That removed the pathological CPU microstalls.
- 10:18 PT: paused KV compaction and re-ran compaction offline against a snapshot; we validated cache integrity.
- 10:30–11:00 PT: gradually rebalanced traffic back on the hosts; p95 returned to ~360ms and 500s dropped to baseline.

Actions going forward:
- We'll ship a non-fused fallback binary to AuroraForge by 2028-03-05 and recommend a coordinated kernel patch backport that avoids the compaction corner-case.
- Follow-up PM: Vivek + AuroraForge infra to run a regeneration job on a staging snapshot to reproduce.
- Naomi/Marissa will prepare a short executive note summarizing impact and credits — draft to AuroraForge exec by EOD.

Thanks for raising this quickly; I'm marking the incident as mitigated but not closed until the patch is applied. Sara — please confirm if your execs want a joint call with our CTO and AuroraForge leadership next week.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
